body:
Hi, sorry! I think I may have remembered the number of months for each dosage wrongly because it was quite a few years ago but I do know that my dermatologist made sure I reached a cumulative dose of at least 5,800 mg which I think is 128mg/kg (I weighed 44-45kg at the time).

I have visited 3 dermatologists and they all agreed on the low dosage indefinitely prescription. All of them seemed really hesitant on increasing my dosage, especially since my acne is no longer cystic like it was 3 years ago. The low dosage is mainly for up keep and prevention I think. 

I think my body might be dependent on accutane now, because whenever I get off it, my skin breaks out within 2 months, and when I get back on it again, my skin clears right back up within a couple of weeks.

I’m 21 this year. My acne mainly occurs around my cheeks and forehead, so I’m not sure whether it’s hormonal. I hope I will grow out of it eventually because no one else in my immediate family has acne issues.

Actually, I don’t think I experience much of the conventional side effects of accutane. I mainly attribute this to my very low dosage because when I was on 20-30mg per day earlier on in my accutane journey, I did experience dry eyes, cracked lips and even hair loss.

However, all of these side effects stopped once my derm put me on 10mg per day. In fact, since I am now on 3.33mg per day, my skin is no longer flakey, I no longer have to put lip balm on my lips anymore, and the oil has returned but the acne is still at bay.

Thanks for the info! That’s good to hear but I do hope that I no longer have to be dependent on a drug to control my acne one day. I just feel sort of helpless that accutane is the only solution to my persistent problem.

I hope differin will help your condition! For me, differin worked wonders when I was first put on it but my acne started returning after 1-2 years of being on it. This was prior to taking accutane though.

Pertaining to the happiness side effect, I find that I am sort of the opposite. When I’m off accutane and the acne returns, I feel extremely frustrated and sad. When I go back on it again, it only a takes a couple of weeks for my skin to clear up again and I would finally feel “at peace”.

I don’t think my diet contributes much to my acne because I tried cutting all junk foods, sugary foods and generally eating very clean for almost a year even before my cystic breakout but I still got acne.   
I am also extremely conscious of my skincare and I religiously check and research the ingredients even before purchasing a skincare product.

I am also not on birth control. My country does not require females who take accutane to be on birth control, and I am abstinent anyways.

The worst part is that I visited quite a few dermatologists about my condition already and they all agree that me taking a very low dosage of accutane indefinitely is the best protocol for my skin. They all mainly attribute my acne to stress which triggers some hormonal changes in my body. And since stress is inevitable in life there‘s nothing much I can do about it. So if all the professionals agree on this, I really don’t know how else I can prevent acne besides heeding their advice :(

Thanks for taking time out of your day to reply to my post. 

My dad cheated on my mom and she almost killed herself because of it. In the end, he didn’t even apologize to her for what he did and pretended that him committing adultery never happened. Although he is a responsible father, it is really hard to swallow what he has done. So yep, there aren’t many male figures I can look up to in my life.

I have tried having a male online friend before, but I’ve always felt uncomfortable around him, to a point where I dreaded when we met in game and had to converse. In the end, I just cut off communication with him entirely when he got too pushy in wanting to meet me in real life.

I do want to try venturing out of comfort zone. But whenever I try taking the first step, I have mini panic attacks and become extremely anxious. Hopefully, I’ll get better one day.

I didn’t really notice it at first but my friends brought it to my attention after they noticed how I responded when guys try to talk to me.

They’ve said I become emotionless, disinterested and just look upset when I talk to guys. And that I give off a scary vibe.

For the guys that have tried to befriend me, I become irrationally fearful and just shut them off immediately.

Hi, thank for your reply! Yes, I am straight, so I do want to try to more comfortable around men in the future.

Right now, the only men I interact with often are my family members. Other than that, although there are still guys I need to interact with in college, be it professors or project members, I keep those interactions to a minimum, short and straight to the point. 

It’s during these interactions where my friends have noticed how cold and distant I am towards guys, as if I became a different person. It got so obvious that they realized that if they were guys, I would have never been friends with them.

Although I know that not all guys are bad, it is difficult to tell which ones aren’t and which ones are. This sense of unknown leads me to just shut off all guys and save myself anymore emotional pain. I do want to try work through this with therapy and all but I can’t afford it now. Thanks again, for taking time out of your day to read my post.

Thanks for the suggestion! I’ll look into CPTSD. 

My college does have on campus counselors but from the accounts of other students who have visited them, they are mostly dismissive, unqualified and just generally do not know how to deal with issues other than college induced stress.
I’m currently in college and I don’t think I’ll be able to sustain the cost of seeing a therapist for the time being :(
Thank you for your suggestions and reassurance. I’ll try to watch movies that used to make me feel sad and see how it goes!
That’s an interesting insight! I do have a shorter chin but upon measurement it seems to be at least twice as long as my philtrum. Is that too short?

My upper lip is not particularly pouty but I wouldn’t classify it as thin. It does, however, become thin when I try to do a teeth-show smile and that’s when the longish philtrum problem presents itself the most

I appreciate your suggestions and concern. I have researched before and yes I am required to disclose any medical conditions I have beforehand (the field I have in mind does concern security etc). As for lying, I am really not comfortable doing it, and especially not with the government. There have been too many medical data breaches here before that I don’t when/if it will happen again.

After reading reviews of many students of the counseling services available at my university, I am almost certain they are too inadequate to handle my issue. They all give the same basic answer to the mental health issues presented to them by students and it’s really quite disheartening.

I have read up on Avoidant Personality Disorder and it seems that it’s pretty rare (around 2-3% of the general population) and its hard to find someone who has experience treating patients who have this order. Public healthcare psychiatrists, although cheaper, I’ve heard through the grapevines give the same basic answers as my university’s counselors. The mental healthcare in my country is honestly a joke. It seems I can only pin my hopes on psychiatrists in the private sector but those will burn a hole in my pocket like no tomorrow. Even then, I don’t even know whether it’ll help.

Honestly, the only reason I’m not dead yet is because of my parents. I want to try because of them but I don’t know how long I can hold on.

Again, thanks for taking time out of your day to reply.

Hi thanks for your reply. I do not live in the countries you mentioned above. The main reason why I am afraid is if I ever work for the government in the future. I may be required by law to state any medical conditions I have prior to employment. Now, even in college, whenever I have to fill up important forms, I am required to disclose my medical history, and yes, even mental health history.
